meta.desktopWiring: desktop/rf_sky_view.py:4246 limit = limit_magnitude(fov,bortle) - twilight_limit_penalty_mag(sun_alt); pinned by tests/test_sky_realism_batch.py::TestTwilightPenalty

formulas.skyBrightnessMagArcsec2: None/NaN/non-finite -> 21.6; alt>=table[0].alt(10) -> table[0].mag(4.0); alt<=table[-1].alt(-90) -> 21.6; else descending-alt segment a_lo<=alt<=a_hi: t=(alt-a_lo)/(a_hi-a_lo), m_lo + t*(m_hi-m_lo)
formulas.composition: effective = base - penalty(sun_alt) [desktop rf_sky_view.py:4246]; baseKernel = limit_magnitude(fov,bortle) depthCap 9.0; baseWeb = min(webDepthCap, naked_eye+detail_gain) depthCap 7.5; web effectiveLimit pins at intro=1 (intro fade is web presentation)

notVerified: sky-brightness table is an order-of-magnitude approximation of published twilight curves (Krisciunas & Schaefer 1991 PASP 103,1033; Patat et al. 2006 A&A 455,385), NOT radiometrically calibrated; aerosol/ozone/latitude/azimuth give ~+/-1 mag
zenith-equivalent brightness only: NO azimuth dependence (sunward sky is much brighter than anti-sunward), NO moonlight term
display-layer only (draw/not-draw, how-dim); never used for pointing / orbit determination / pass conclusions
sun_alt input on the web comes from a low-precision analytic solar position (Meeus simplified, ~+/-0.5 deg, not a precise ephemeris); the penalty inherits that input uncertainty
web depthCap=7.5 (HYG cutoff) shallower than kernel CATALOG_DEPTH_MAG=9.0; applied at the 31-celestial call site, not in the kernel mirror
intro dark-adaptation fade is a web presentation layer; composition pinned at intro=1
full sky-brightness photometric model (moon phase / actual calibrated sky surface brightness) still NOT implemented (kernel limitations-register L24)
